Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

transform verb

also turn into, change into, convert, convert into, transformation

classical

Plaut. Am. prol. 121: Juppiter in Amphitruōnis vortit sēsē imāginem (Lewis & Short)
Lucr. 2.880 (Lewis & Short)

vertō, vertere, vertī, versum

verb, third conjugation; in + accusative; sē vertere, to turn oneself into · Conjugation on Wiktionary

turn; change, transform

To turn something into something else, in with the accusative (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • convertō, convertere, convertī, conversum — change the nature of, transform

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Ov. M. 1.88: tellūs induit ignōtās hominum conversa figūrās (Lewis & Short) · Conjugation on Wiktionary

    First to turn round; then to change the nature of a thing (Lewis & Short).

  • trānsfōrmō, trānsfōrmāre, trānsfōrmāvī, trānsfōrmātum — change in shape, transform

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Verg. G. 4.441: omnia trānsfōrmat sēsē in mīrācula rērum (Lewis & Short) · Conjugation on Wiktionary

    (vōx plērumque poētica: Verg., Ov.; then post-Augustan prose)

    Change of outward shape, as in Ovid’s tales; Quintilian uses it of the mind taking on the nature of its subject (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • Juppiter in Amphitruōnis vortit sēsē imāginem

    Jupiter turns himself into the likeness of AmphitryonPlaut. Am. prol. 121 (Lewis & Short)

  • omnia trānsfōrmat sēsē in mīrācula rērum

    he turns himself into every wonder in the worldVerg. G. 4.441 (Lewis & Short)

  • mūtārī in (+ accusative)

    to turn intoTraupman 399

See also change, become.
